questions.prompt: Which territory, after voting to join Iturbide's empire in 1822, declared its independence from Mexico on 1 July 1823?
options: Central America
Yucatán
Texas
Alta California
questions.explanation: Mexican troops under Vicente Filísola had occupied El Salvador to enforce the union. After Iturbide fell, a congress in Guatemala City declared the provinces independent, creating the United Provinces of Central America, while Chiapas, after briefly declaring itself free, opted for Mexico in 1824.

questions.prompt: What kind of state did Mexico's first constitution, of 1824, create?
options: A federal republic of states and territories
A centralist republic governed from the capital
A constitutional empire under a Bourbon prince
A republic joined with the provinces of Central America
questions.explanation: The constitution also made Catholicism the sole permitted religion. The tension between federalists, who wanted strong states, and centralists, who wanted a strong capital, shaped the next three decades and much of the territorial loss.

questions.prompt: In which year did the last Spanish garrison, in the island fortress of San Juan de Ulúa off Veracruz, finally capitulate?
questions.explanation: Spain did not accept the Treaty of Córdoba, and in 1823 the garrison bombarded Veracruz for three months. Mexico bought warships with its London loans, and a blockade under Pedro Sáinz de Baranda kept relief from Cuba away until the last defenders gave up in November 1825; Spain tried to reconquer the country at Tampico in 1829.

questions.prompt: Where did Santa Anna's army storm the Alamo, the former mission of San Antonio de Valero at Béxar, in March 1836? Click the map.
questions.explanation: The army stormed the Alamo on 6 March, killing nearly all of its defenders; the Texas convention had declared independence at Washington-on-the-Brazos four days earlier. With the Goliad massacre later that month, it became a rallying cry for the Texan army.

questions.prompt: Captured after San Jacinto, what did Santa Anna agree to in the Treaties of Velasco of May 1836?
options: To withdraw beyond the Rio Grande and work for Texan recognition
To pay 600,000 pesos to settle the claims of French nationals
To promise US citizenship to Mexicans who stayed in Texas
To abolish slavery in Texas and free the people held there
questions.explanation: Sam Houston's army had routed Santa Anna's camp at San Jacinto in under twenty minutes. On 20 May the government in Mexico City declared void all acts Santa Anna performed as a captive, and Mexico continued to regard Texas as a rebel province.

questions.prompt: From the 1830s, which raiders rode south each autumn across the Rio Grande and struck as deep as Durango, Zacatecas and San Luis Potosí?
options: Comanche and Kiowa war parties
Yaqui and Mayo fighters under Juan Banderas
Texans of the Santa Fe Expedition
Filibusters under William Walker
questions.explanation: In December 1840 some four hundred riders reached San Luis Potosí and attacked Saltillo on the way back. The raids killed and captured thousands and emptied much of the north of settlers and resources before the US invasion.

questions.prompt: Which disputed land became the trigger of the US–Mexican War in 1846?
options: The strip between the Nueces and the Rio Grande
The Mesilla Valley south of New Mexico
Soconusco, on the Pacific coast of Chiapas
The coast around Fort Ross, north of San Francisco
questions.explanation: Under Spain and Mexico the province of Texas ended at the Nueces, but Texas, and then the United States, claimed to the Rio Grande. Polk ordered Zachary Taylor into the strip, and the clash there in April 1846 gave him his claim that Mexico had "shed American blood upon the American soil".

questions.prompt: Where did Commodore John D. Sloat land sailors and marines at Monterey, the capital of Alta California, in July 1846? Click the map.
questions.explanation: Sloat proclaimed the annexation of California on 7 July, a few weeks after American settlers had proclaimed a "California Republic" at Sonoma. Resistance by Californios in the south later drove US forces out of Los Angeles for several months.

questions.prompt: What did Mexico cede to the United States by the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo in 1848?
options: Alta California and New Mexico
Baja California and Sonora
Chiapas and Soconusco
The Mesilla Valley and land south of the Gila
questions.explanation: In return for $15 million and the assumption of claims, Mexico gave up about half of its claimed territory, counting Texas; gold had been found in California nine days before the signing. Because the treaty map misplaced El Paso and the Rio Grande, New Mexico's southern boundary stayed disputed until Santa Anna sold the Mesilla strip in 1853.

questions.prompt: Where did rebel Maya capture Valladolid, one of Yucatán's principal cities, in the spring of 1848? Click the map.
questions.explanation: The Caste War had begun in July 1847 when Cecilio Chi attacked the town of Tepich. At its height the rebels advanced to within a short distance of Mérida and Campeche before withdrawing at planting time, and Yucatán, which had broken away in 1841, rejoined Mexico in 1848 in exchange for military aid.
